and executable tests are canonical after implementation. Ticket numbers are
shared across the release-polish plans; these continue from POLISH-038.

The tickets come from the 2026-11-05 audit (commit `555d895`). Each names the
audit finding it closes; the report lives outside git under
`data/polish-audit/2026-11-05.md`, and everything an implementer needs is
restated here and in the spec.

## Tickets

### POLISH-039: The Preview tab always answers

**Status**

Complete on 2026-11-05. A `channel_unschedulable` refusal now reads "This
channel has no shows yet. Add shows on the Lineup tab." with no shows, and
the channel's off-air words for any other reason, on the Preview tab and in
the special editor's Preview; nothing deferred.

**Goal**: A channel whose shows cannot air gets owner words with a next step
on the Preview tab and in the special editor's Preview, never "The channel
cannot generate a schedule". Closes UI-unschedulable-refusal-verbatim.

**Scope**: Add a `channel_unschedulable` case to `codeWords` in
`apps/web/src/http/refusal-words.ts` keyed on `details.reason`:
`no_programming_assignment` → "This channel has no shows yet. Add shows on
the Lineup tab."; `no_schedulable_media` → `offAirWords("schedule_gap")`.
Both render sites already go through `RequestFeedback`, so no component
changes beyond the test.

**Out of scope**: Changing when the server refuses; the schedule route's
own copy of the sentence (never shown by the web).

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**: The server sets the reason at
`packages/krazi-brain/src/krazi-plan/generate-programming.ts:278-284` and
forwards it from `programming-preview-routes.ts` and `reservation-routes.ts`.
An unknown reason falls back to the off-air words, never to the server's
sentence.

**Verification**: `npm test --workspace @krazitv/web`: one jsdom test per
reason for the Preview tab, one for the special editor's Preview.

**Docs impact**: None; the wiki already describes the off-air words.

### POLISH-040: Continuing turns and the random reset

**Status**

Complete on 2026-11-05. The Preview tab leads a turn already on the air with
"continues at <time>" and counts what it has left as more, and a Random
show's Up Next reset reads **Reshuffle…** with its own question; ordered
modes keep their words.

**Goal**: A turn already under way reads as continuing, and a Random show's
reset says what it does. Closes UI-preview-continued-turn-reads-already-airing
and UI-restart-wording-under-random.

**Scope**: In `turnWords`, a turn with `continues` leads with "continues at
<time>" and words its remaining programs as "1 more episode" (or "N more
programs"), instead of listing the time first and "already airing" last; the
line renderer in `upcoming-programming.tsx` passes the time in rather than
prefixing it. In `collection-preview-section.tsx` and
`progress-reset-dialog.tsx`, when the mode is random the button reads
**Reshuffle…**, the dialog title "Reshuffle", and the question "Start
<name>'s random picks over on this channel? What is airing now finishes; the
schedule after it is rebuilt." Ordered modes keep today's words.

**Out of scope**: The server's preview contract; the Up Next list itself.

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**: `modeLabel` is already a prop of the reset dialog.
Keep the time formatting in `displayListTime`.

**Verification**: `npm test --workspace @krazitv/web`: a jsdom test renders
a continuing turn and reads "continues at"; one renders the Up Next tab for a
random show and reads the button and the question; the existing ordered-mode
tests still read "Restart from the beginning".

**Docs impact**: `wiki/My-Channels.md` and `wiki/Play-Order.md` where they
name the reset button.

### POLISH-041: Remaining owner words

**Status**

Complete on 2026-11-05. The Add media root field reads "Folder on the kraziTV
server", Live Monitor says "See what each channel is airing right now", the
web words `internal_error`, `schedule_busy`, `programming_assignment_not_found`,
and `media_root_removal_pending` (its time through `displayTime`), and the
folder browser's path refusal names its field. The server already sent
`airingUntil` as an API timestamp, so it was kept rather than changed to
milliseconds.

**Goal**: The last two web strings and the five server refusals an owner can
trigger read in owner words. Closes the UI-developer-words-remain residual.

**Scope**: Relabel the Add media root field "Folder on the kraziTV server"
and the Live Monitor program "See what each channel is airing right now".
Add `codeWords` cases for `internal_error`, `schedule_busy`,
`programming_assignment_not_found`, and `media_root_removal_pending` with the
sentences in the spec; the last reads the time from `details.airingUntil`
through `displayTime`. On the server, `media_root_removal_pending` adds
`airingUntil` (integer milliseconds) to its details, and the folders route's
path refusal sends `fields: [{ path: "path", code: "custom" }]` so the
existing path sentence applies.

**Out of scope**: Other `invalid_request` fall-throughs that no UI action
reaches.

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**: The server's `message` stays for logs and API
users; only `details` grow. The spec 0002 grep target and the browser walk's
"Absolute server path" assertion, if any, move with the label.

**Verification**: `npm test --workspace @krazitv/server` for the two detail
changes; `npm test --workspace @krazitv/web` with one jsdom test per code;
grep `apps/web/src` for "Absolute" and "channel state" in user-visible
strings finds nothing.

**Docs impact**: `wiki/Media-Library.md` (the field label),
`wiki/The-Desktop.md` and `wiki/Live-Monitor.md` (the description),
`wiki/Troubleshooting.md` if it quotes a refusal.

### POLISH-042: One-line Lineup rows, unbroken paths, formatted counts

**Status**

Complete on 2026-11-05. Play order, At a time, and Marathons are
`narrow-column` cells while Show and the owner-named Rules wrap, dialog bodies
break a path anywhere, and collection cards, the editor's save bar, and
Discover collections count members through one `itemCountWords`. Rules stays
an ordinary column rather than nowrap, since rule names are uncapped.

**Goal**: The Lineup table reads one row per show at the default window
size, dialog paragraphs never scroll sideways, and every count has thousands
separators. Closes UI-lineup-columns-wrap-at-default-size,
UI-dialog-paragraph-unbroken-path, and UI-raw-count-in-cards.

**Scope**: `narrow-column` on the Play order and At a time cells in
`lineup-tab.tsx`; Marathons and Rules columns sized to content (a `1%`
width or the same class). `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `.window-dialog-body`
in `controls.css`. `displayCount` at the three count sites (collection card,
editor save bar, Discover dialog).

**Out of scope**: Hiding the Marathons and Rules columns when empty; the
dialog width.

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**: Check the Show column still ellipsizes or wraps a
60-character name rather than pushing the action button off the row. The
`overflow-wrap` rule must not break the Discover dialog's cards or the
special preview's list.

**Verification**: `npm test --workspace @krazitv/web`: a jsdom test asserts
the two cells carry the class; one renders the Delete media root sentence
with a 75-character unbroken path and asserts `overflow-wrap`; one renders a
1,284-member card and reads "1,284 items". The browser walk gains one
assertion that no Lineup row is taller than two text lines at 640 wide.

**Docs impact**: None; screenshots refresh in POLISH-053.

### POLISH-043: Enter in the special editor and desktop arrow keys

**Status**

Complete on 2026-11-05. The special editor is a form whose Enter presses
Preview while no preview is current and Save special once one is, and
Start's arrow-key navigation moved to `desktop/arrow-navigation.ts`, which
Start and the desktop icons share, gaining Home and End in both.

**Goal**: Enter works in the one dialog where it is dead, and the desktop
icons move with the arrows as Start's items do. Closes
UI-special-editor-enter and UI-desktop-shortcut-arrow-keys.

**Scope**: Wrap the special editor's fields in a `<form>` whose submit runs
the preview while none is current and the save otherwise; **Preview** and
**Save special** become `type="submit"` in that order, **Add a program** and
**Cancel** stay `type="button"`. Lift `navigate` out of `start-menu.tsx` to a
shared place both callers import (beside the shell, not a `utils` folder) and
attach it to `.desktop-shortcuts` with Up, Down, Home, End.

**Out of scope**: Arrow keys on the taskbar (Tab-only, as XP's was).

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**: The date field submits on Enter natively once a
form exists; make sure the `select` for Program N does not. `navigate` takes
a column model today; the desktop is one column.

**Verification**: `npm test --workspace @krazitv/web`: a jsdom test presses
Enter in Starts and sees the preview requested, then Enter again after a
preview and sees the save; one presses Down on the first desktop icon and
sees the second focused, End the last.

**Docs impact**: `wiki/The-Desktop.md` (keyboard line) and
`wiki/Specials.md` if it says to press Preview.

### POLISH-044: Names capped at 120

**Status**

Complete on 2026-11-05. Channel and collection names past 120 characters are
refused with `too_big` through a `longNameField` beside `nameField`, and the
web's one name sentence names each cap: 120 for a channel or collection, 80
for a show. Rule names are still uncapped on the server (the Rule dialog
holds 80); that is left for a later ticket.

**Goal**: A channel or collection name longer than 120 characters is refused
with the words the web already has (decision 18).

**Scope**: A `.max(120)` on the channel and collection name fields (a
`longNameField` beside `nameField` in `request-schemas.ts`, or the cap on
`nameField` itself if every caller agrees; show and rule names keep 80). The
web's `FIELD_WORDS.name.too_big` names the limit.

**Out of scope**: Trimming or truncating existing names; the account display
name (40).

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**: `nameField` is shared by several routes; read each
caller before raising the cap on the shared field.

**Verification**: `npm test --workspace @krazitv/server`: a 121-character
channel name and collection name are refused with `too_big`; `npm test
--workspace @krazitv/web` reads the sentence.

**Docs impact**: None.

### POLISH-046: A scan that finds nothing says what kraziTV looks for

**Status**

Complete on 2026-11-05. The media package exports its one supported
extension list, every completed scan summary carries it, and a scan that
finds no files reads "No video files found. kraziTV looks for .mkv, .mp4,
… in this folder and its subfolders." naming all seven extensions; the
list is short enough that no "and N more" tooltip was needed.

**Goal**: An owner who scanned the wrong folder learns what to point at
(decision 16).

**Scope**: Export the accepted extension list from the media package's
discovery module, carry it on the scan status or summary the server already
sends, and in `scan-progress-dialog.tsx` when a finished scan has

### POLISH-054: Reshuffle starts a new order

**Status**

Complete on 2026-11-06. A random show's progress reset now counts into its
collection's seed (migration 036), so **Reshuffle…** gives a new order that
still repeats for the same inputs, a count of 0 keeps every channel's
existing order, and the dialog words it without a possessive; nothing
deferred.

**Goal**: **Reshuffle…** on a random show gives a new, still repeatable
random order, as its label promises (decision 19).

**Scope**:

- kraziBrain: the collection's random seed derives from the channel seed,
  the collection, and the progress reset count (`deriveCollectionSeed` in
  `packages/krazi-brain/src/schedule/seeded-hash.ts`, its callers in
  `playback-selection.ts` and `generate-schedule-entries.ts`, and whatever
  computes a random show's upcoming picks for Up Next). A count of 0 must
  give exactly today's seed, so pulling this change reorders no channel
  until its owner reshuffles.
- Server: migration 036 adds a reset count (integer, not null, default 0)
  to `channel_collection_progress`; `resetProgress` in
  `apps/server/src/schedules/persistence/collection-progress.ts` increments
  it; generation, restoration, and the upcoming-selections route pass the
  current count to kraziBrain, so an earlier order never returns.
- Web: `progress-reset-dialog.tsx` words the random case as the spec says
  ("Reshuffle Suits on this channel? Its random picks start over in a new
  order. …" and "Suits plays in a new random order after what is airing
  now. Upcoming selections:"), with no possessive built from the name.
- `GLOSSARY.md`'s **Progress reset** row says a random reset starts a new
  seeded order; `wiki/Play-Order.md` (the Random paragraph and Starting
  over) says the same.

**Out of scope**: Ordered modes; the fresh rebuild; how random draws with
replacement.

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**: Backend first (kraziBrain and server), then the
web on top on the same branch. Programming spec 0003 is historical; record
the change through decision 19, the glossary, and tests, not by rewriting 0003. Determinism: same channel seed, collection, count, and index give
the same pick.

**Verification**: A kraziBrain test: picks after a reset differ from those
before it, a count of 0 matches today's seed, and two runs agree. A server
test: reset, regenerate, and the new order holds. A migration test for 036.
A jsdom test reads both sentences. The full gate.

**Docs impact**: `wiki/Play-Order.md`, `GLOSSARY.md`.

## Sequencing

| Wave | Tickets                                                     | Who                                            |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | POLISH-039, 040, 041, 042, 043, 044                         | web-engineer (044 with backend-engineer)       |
| 2    | POLISH-045, 046, 047, 048, 049 (web); 050, 051 (kinds); 052 | web-engineer, backend-engineer, media-engineer |
| 3    | POLISH-053                                                  | docs-maintainer                                |
| 4    | POLISH-054, 056 (backend then web); 057, 058, 059, 061      | backend-engineer, web-engineer                 |
| 5    | POLISH-055 (backend then web); 060                          | backend-engineer, web-engineer                 |
| 6    | POLISH-062                                                  | docs-maintainer                                |

Wave 1 closes every audit finding on the first-run screens and can ship as
one release candidate. Wave 2 starts from main after wave 1 merges, so the
shortcuts and the kinds see wave 1's edits to `refusal-words.ts`,
`start-menu.tsx`, and the wiki. Wave 3 waits for both, so the screenshot
refresh runs once. The second round's wave 5 waits for wave 4 because
POLISH-055 follows POLISH-056 in the same refusal files and takes the next
migration, and POLISH-060 moves files POLISH-058 and 059 edit; wave 6 waits
for both.
